analysis.d_full: THE ARCHIVE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'PennSound is the world's largest free digital archive of poetry audio, featuring over 50,000 recordings spanning from 1913 to the present.' Overview & Mission (CPCW and the Kelly Writers House; the three directors; singles; scope from Williams, Stevens, Stein and Eliot to contemporary poets); Key Features (author pages, 'the Charles Ruas Author Page'; podcasts and PennSound Rewind 'hosted by Michael Hennessey'; PoemTalk with Jacket2; 'open-access and noncommercial'). Twelve cards: CPCW, Jacket2, Wikipedia, YouTube (four), poets.org, Penn Today, X, Instagram, ModPo.
findings: HOST AND DIRECTORS EXACT. 'Co-directed by Al Filreis, Charles Bernstein, and Chris Mustazza.' The about page: 'Charles Bernstein , Al Filreis , and Chris Mustazza , Directors' and 'PennSound is a project of the Center for Programs in Contemporary Writing.' Michael Hennessey, the about page's 'Editor', is named as host of PennSound Rewind (the home page: 'at our new PennSound Rewind page and at Jacket2.org'). The new Charles Ruas collection is carried ('recent additions like the Charles Ruas Author Page featuring historical radio interviews'); the home page announced 'a new home for Charles Ruas's radio programming from the 70s, 80s, and 00s', 'Posted 3/27/2026'. The 2005 launch is not carried.

THE COUNT. 'over 50,000 recordings spanning from 1913 to the present' follows the Instagram card and the saved article's 'Well over 50,000 sound files', and the 1913 the home page's 'Guillaume Apollinaire, "Le Pont Mirabeau" (1913)'. The same article gives 'over 1500 full-length and single-poem recordings'; the composition calls all the files recordings. Of the four poets it names in its scope, T.S. Eliot appears in none of the three saved PennSound pages.

THE CREDITS NOT CARRIED. The census row reads PennSound as a witness of a distinct type, where author, performer and co-composer are credited apart: 'John Clare, "Vowelless Letter" (1849) performed by Charles Bernstein', 'Hannah Weiner, from Clairvoyant Journal , performed by Weiner, Sharon Mattlin & Rochelle Kraut', 'the music and performance is by Christopher Reiner (and included with permission)'. The composition files everything under 'Author Pages: Extensive, individual catalogs for thousands of writers', matching the manifesto rule the article reports ('Sound files must be indexed and retrievable from a library catalog under the poet’s name'), and has no place for a reading of one poet's work by another.

Archive Access: All audio files are open-access and noncommercial.

* Host & Location: Based at the University of Pennsylvania's Center for Programs in Contemporary Writing (CPCW) and associated with the [Kelly Writers House](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESUgHrOzAVr8uUV5erVkfAVbOIkt_HVL3Up84WQN9vwxjtmjBbov1j_HnxN4uWPrt6wtISDGkGukw1FCER9nw2EnVW9YrBwEXLPGR9eimpxfzQiPE).
